subject: Computer Science
whyScene: The core idea is a comparison of shapes across a range of n. A log-log plot makes growth classes visible as slopes, and a moving curve lets the learner see that a constant multiplier translates a line without rotating it. Text alone would force the learner to imagine the chart and would hide the crossover.
objective: Compare n, n log n and n squared growth, and explain why constant factors are secondary asymptotically.
learner: Can read functions and small tables; new to asymptotic notation.

misconceptions.counter: The vertical axis is operation count as a function of n. The scene never converts to time; the final checkpoint says Big-O names a class, not a stopwatch reading.
The 1000n line lifts three decades but stays parallel to n. It still meets n squared at n = 1000 and is overtaken afterwards, so the constant delays the crossover without changing the class.

teachingSequence.teacher: Name the two axes and the three curves; point out that both axes are logarithmic, so slope is the growth class.
teachingSequence.learner: Locates n, n log n and n squared and says which is flattest and which is steepest.
teachingSequence.evidence: Learner states the ordering n < n log n < n squared before any number is computed.

teachingSequence.teacher: Introduce a constant multiplier of 1000 and slide the 1000n line up three decades.
teachingSequence.learner: Predicts whether the lifted line changes class; checks that it stays parallel to n.
teachingSequence.evidence: Learner says the slope is unchanged, so the class is unchanged.

teachingSequence.teacher: Hold at n = 1000, where 1000n and n squared both equal one million, then look to the right of the crossover.
teachingSequence.learner: Explains why a big constant can win for small n but cannot win asymptotically.
teachingSequence.evidence: Learner distinguishes 'wins for a while' from 'belongs to a slower class'.

teachingSequence.teacher: State that Big-O discards constant factors and lower-order terms and describes an upper bound as n grows.
teachingSequence.learner: Restates the definition without a timing claim.
teachingSequence.evidence: Learner avoids seconds and avoids saying the constant is irrelevant at every n.

interactionDesign: The learner advances through four checkpoints. The key manipulative is the constant multiplier: the 1000n line animates from the n line (factor 1) to its lifted position (factor 1000), so the invariant slope is visible during the change. Narration supplies the numerical readings at n = 10, 100 and 1000 that the logarithmic axes cannot show as tick labels.

sceneBrief.view: Log-log chart from n = 1 to n = 10,000 and from 1 to 10^8 operations.
sceneBrief.marks: Blue n line, black n log n polyline, red n squared line, and a blue 1000n line that starts on top of n and lifts.
sceneBrief.motion: The 1000n line and its endpoint label rise by three decades between t = 2 and t = 8 while remaining parallel to n.
sceneBrief.labels: Each curve is labelled at its right end; the constant line is labelled at its moving left end.
sceneBrief.reading: At n = 1000 the 1000n line crosses n squared; to the right, n squared is above it.

accessibility: All information is also in the narration, checkpoint bodies and fallback text; colour is never the only signal because every curve is directly labelled. reducedMotion is static, keyboard is true, and the chart is described in alt text.
fidelityChecks: Asymptotic order n < n log n < n squared is correct.
Multiplying by 1000 changes the intercept, not the slope or the class.
No claim about seconds, hardware or measured runtime.
The crossover at n = 1000 is arithmetically correct: 1000n = n squared = 1,000,000.
